''' Howard Ensign Simmons Jr.''' (June 17, 1929 &ndash; April 26, 1997) was an American chemist, who studied at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], before starting a long career at [[DuPont]], who with his workmate Ronald D. Smith discovered the [[Simmons–Smith reaction]].

==Biography==
Simmons was born on June 17, 1929, in [[Norfolk, Virginia|Norfolk]], Virginia and was an only child. His father was a [[sea captain|Sea Captain]] and his mother was a descendant of [[Jacob Hübner]]. Growing up he had a [[laboratory]] at home which he began conducting [[Experiment|experiments]] in at the age of 12.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Jefferson |first=Edward G. |date=1999 |title=Howard Ensign Simmons, Jr. (17 June 1929-26 April 1997) |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/3182000 |journal=Proceedings of the American Philosophical Society |volume=143 |issue=4 |pages=719–726 |issn=0003-049X|via=JSTOR}}</ref>

Despite winning a scholarship to attend the [[University of Virginia|University of Virgina]], he instead decided to study at MIT and gained a bachelor's degree in [[chemistry]] in 1951, where he minored in mathematics and physics, remaining at MIT to complete his post graduate education,<ref name=":1" /> and conducting his research under Jack D. Roberts and [[Arthur C. Cope]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=1993-04-27 |title=Oral history interview with Howard E. Simmons, Jr. |url=https://digital.sciencehistory.org/works/2r36tz72w |access-date=2026-08-20 |website=Science History Institute Digital Collections |language=en}}</ref>

By 1954 he had completed his doctorate and he accepted an offer to join DuPont.<ref name=":1" /> Simmons worked in DuPonts Central Research and Development department,<ref name=":1" /> beginning research into [[polyacetylene]] before moving onto [[Fluoroacetone|fluoroketone]].<ref name=":2" /> During his career at DuPont, he and his colleague Ronald D. Smith discovered the Simmons-Smith reaction,<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last= |date= |title=The Priestley Medal was awarded to Howard E. Simmons |url=https://lifesciencehistory.com/the-priestley-medal-was-awarded-to-howard-e-simmons/ |access-date=2026-08-20 |website=LifeScienceHistory.com |language=en-US}}</ref> and published a journal about it in 1958.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date= |title=Simmons-Smith Reaction: Definition, Mechanism, and Examples |url=https://www.chemistrylearner.com/simmons-smith-reaction.html |access-date=2026-08-20 |website=Chemistry Learner |language=en-US}}</ref> By 1959 Simmons had been promoted to be a Supervisor at DuPont.<ref name=":1" />

In 1976, Simmons served as Chair of the organic division of the [[American Chemical Society]].<ref name="HES01">[https://www.organicdivision.org/history/ ACS Organic Division History.] - Retrieved 2018-9-24.</ref> He was a member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=Howard Ensign Simmons|url=https://www.amacad.org/person/howard-ensign-simmons|access-date=2022-02-10|website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences|language=en}}</ref> the [[National Academy of Sciences]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=H. E. Simmons Jr.|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/h-e-simmons-jr-ic3dom/|access-date=2022-02-10|website=www.nasonline.org}}</ref> and the [[American Philosophical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=APS Member History|url=https://search.amphilsoc.org/memhist/search?creator=Howard+E.+Simmons&title=&subject=&subdiv=&mem=&year=&year-max=&dead=&keyword=&smode=advanced|access-date=2022-02-10|website=search.amphilsoc.org}}</ref>

He retired from DuPont in 1992, after becoming Vice President, and the same year as he was given the National Medal of Science by [[George H. W. Bush|President Bush]],<ref name=":1" /> due to his "fundamental contributions to synthesis, [[molecular structure]], and the theory of [[organic chemistry]], and for his productive management of the premier industrial chemical research program in the United States".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Santisi |first=Jennifer |title=Howard E. Simmons Jr. |url=https://nationalmedals.org/laureate/howard-e-simmons-jr/ |access-date=2026-08-20 |website=National Science and Technology Medals Foundation |language=en-US}}</ref>

The American Chemical Society awarded him the Priestley Medal for his contributions to chemistry,<ref name=":0" /> and DuPont awarded him the Lavoisier Medal, in 1994.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Schulz |first=William |date=1997-05-12 |title=Howard Simmons, former DuPont executive, dies at 67 |url=https://dx.doi.org/10.1021/cen-v075n019.p014a |journal=Chemical & Engineering News Archive |language=en |volume=75 |issue=19 |pages=14–14 |doi=10.1021/cen-v075n019.p014a |issn=0009-2347|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

He was a heavy smoker for most of his life and developed lung cancer and heart disease.<ref name=":0" /> He died on April 26, 1997.<ref name=":1" />
